And one may say: The hadith you narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam is problematic, for the apparent meaning of the hadith gives the impression that when he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the three questions, the answers were given by the Prophet (ﷺ) to ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam because the Prophet (ﷺ) had mentioned those answers. And this is very far-fetched, for two reasons:

The first: informing about the first sign of the Hour and about the first food the people of Paradise will eat is informing about the occurrence of something among the possibilities, and for such a matter it is not known that the report is true unless it is first known that the informant is truthful. So if we knew the truthfulness of the informant by the truth of that report, it would lead to circular reasoning (dawr), and that is impossible.

**Second point:** We know by necessity that the answers given to these questions do not reach the level of being a miracle at all. Rather, we say: skilled answers to difficult questions do not reach the level of a miracle, so how can it be said that such answers to such questions reached the level of a miracle? The answer is that it is possible that it came in some of the books of the earlier Prophets that the Messenger of the last age would be asked these questions and would answer them with these answers. 'Abd Allah ibn Salam knew this meaning. When he asked the Prophet ﷺ and he answered with those answers, he recognised by this means that he was truly a Messenger from Allah. On this basis there is no need for us to say that knowledge of these answers is a miracle. And Allah knows best.

**Second opinion:** Concerning the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And a witness from the Children of Israel testified﴾, it is said that the intended meaning is not a specific individual. Rather, the intended meaning is that the mention of Muhammad ﷺ is present in the Torah, and the good tidings of his coming are contained in it. So the sense of the speech is: if a fair-minded man who knows the Torah acknowledged this and affirmed it, then he believed in Muhammad ﷺ while you denied him, would you not have been wrongdoers against yourselves, astray from the truth? This statement holds firm whether the intended witness is a specific person or not, because the primary purpose of this speech is that it has been established by compelling miracles that this Book is from Allah, and it has been established that the Torah contains the good tidings of the coming of Muhammad ﷺ. With these two matters, how does it befit reason to deny his prophethood?

**Third issue:** Concerning the saying of the Exalted: ﴿upon the like of it﴾, the commentators have offered several views. The closest is that he ﷺ said to them: Tell me, if this Qur'an is from Allah as I say, and a witness from the Children of Israel testified to the like of what I have said, ﴿then he believed while you were arrogant﴾, were you not wrongdoers against yourselves?

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. On this there are several issues.

**First issue:** This is a threat, and it stands in place of the omitted answer. The estimated sense is: Say, tell me, if it is from Allah and then you disbelieve in it, you will not be guided, but rather you will be astray.

**Second issue:** The Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school) said: this verse indicates that Allah only withheld guidance from them on account of the evil act that proceeded from them first. For the saying of the Exalted, ﴿Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, is explicit that He does not guide them because they are wrongdoers against themselves. So it is necessary that they hold, regarding all the verses that come concerning the prevention of faith and guidance, that the case is as it is here. And Allah knows best.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe: Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾. On this there are several issues.

**First issue:** This is another doubt of the people in denying the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are several reports.

The first: This is the speech of the disbelievers of Makkah. They said: most of those who follow Muhammad are the poor and the lowly, like 'Ammar, Suhayb and Ibn Mas'ud. Had this religion been good, these would not have preceded us to it.

The second: It is said that when Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Aslam and Ghifar embraced Islam, Banu 'Amir, Ghatafan, Asad and Ash'ar said: Had this been good, the shepherds of the sheep would not have preceded us to it.

The third: It is said that a slave-girl of 'Umar embraced Islam, and 'Umar used to beat her until he grew weary, and he would say: Were it not that I have grown weary, I would have increased your beating. So the disbelievers of Quraysh would say: Had what Muhammad calls to been true, such-and-such a woman would not have preceded us to it.

The fourth: It is said that the Jews used to say this saying when 'Abd Allah ibn Salam embraced Islam.

**Second issue:** Concerning the lam in the saying of the Exalted, ﴿to those who believe﴾, the commentators mention two possibilities.

The first: the meaning is: ﴿those who disbelieve say to those who believe﴾ in the manner of direct address, as you say: Zayd said to 'Amr, and then you leave the direct address and shift to the third person, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them﴾ [Yunus: 22].

The second: the author of al-Kashshaf said: ﴿to those who believe﴾ means "on their account", meaning that the disbelievers said on account of the faith of those who believed: Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it. I have a third view on this: when the disbelievers heard that a group had believed in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they addressed a group of the present believers and said to them: Had this religion been good, those absent ones who embraced Islam would not have preceded us to it.

Know that when the Exalted related this speech of theirs, He answered it with His saying: ﴿And since they have not been guided by it, they will say: This is an ancient falsehood﴾. The meaning is that since they did not come to know the manner in which it is a miracle, there must be an operator for the adverbial phrase in His saying ﴿since they have not been guided by it﴾, and a complement for His saying ﴿they will say﴾. It is not sound that ﴿they will say﴾ is the operator of the adverbial phrase, because the indications of past and future would contradict each other. So what is the sense of this speech? He answered this by saying that the operator of ﴿idh﴾ ("since") is omitted, being indicated by the context, and the estimate is: ﴿And since they have not been guided by it﴾, their obstinacy became apparent, ﴿so they will say: This is an ancient falsehood﴾.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy﴾. "The Book of Moses" is the subject (mubtada'), "before it" is an adverbial phrase functioning as a fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam), and His saying ﴿a guide﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), like your saying: "In the house is Zayd standing." It has also been read as ﴿And before it the Book of Moses﴾. The estimate is: We gave the one before it the Torah. The meaning of ﴿a guide﴾ is: a model to be followed in the religion of Allah and its laws, as one follows an imam. ﴿And a mercy﴾ means: for whoever believes in it and acts by what is in it. The connection of this speech to what precedes it is that the people criticised the soundness of the Qur'an and said: Had it been good, these paupers would not have preceded us to it. It is as if the Exalted said: What indicates the soundness of the Qur'an is that you do not dispute that Allah sent down the Torah to Moses, peace be upon him, and made this Book a guide to be followed. Then the Torah contains the good tidings of the coming of Muhammad ﷺ. So when you concede that the Torah is a guide to be followed, then accept its judgement that Muhammad ﷺ is true from Allah.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And this is a Book confirming in Arabic tongue﴾, that is: this Qur'an confirms the Book of Moses in that Muhammad is truly a Messenger from Allah. The saying of the Exalted ﴿in Arabic tongue﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state. Then He said: ﴿to warn those who did wrong﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: the polytheists of Makkah. In His saying "to warn" (li-tundhira) there are two readings: the "ta" (you) because of the frequency with which this meaning occurs in direct address, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿that you may warn by it, and a reminder for the believers﴾ [al-A'raf: 2]; and the "ya" (he/it) because the Book was mentioned earlier, so the warning is attributed to the Book, just as it is attributed to the Messenger, and in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1], up to His saying: ﴿to warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾ [al-Kahf: 2].

Then the Exalted said: ﴿and good tidings for the good-doers﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the better view is that His saying ﴿and good tidings﴾ is in the nominative position, and the meaning is: it is good tidings for the good-doers. He said: it is also permissible that it be in the accusative position, meaning: to warn those who did wrong, and (to give) good tidings to the good-doers. The sum of the speech is that the purpose of sending down this Book is to warn those who turn away and to give good tidings to those who obey.

[p. 8]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a plain warner.﴾ ﴿Say: Have you considered: if this is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel bears witness to its like and believes, while you act arrogantly, [then what?] Indeed Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe: "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it." And since they have not been guided by it, they will say: "This is an ancient lie."﴾ ﴿And before it was the Book of Musa, a guide and a mercy. And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the good-doers.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, related about them that they [doubted] the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, by saying that he fabricates it from his own self and then attributes it to being the word of Allah as a slander, He related about them another kind of doubt: that they used to demand from him astonishing, overpowering miracles and asked him to inform them of unseen matters. So Allah, exalted is He, answered them by saying: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers.﴾ Al-bid' and al-badi' of anything mean its origin, and al-bid'ah (innovation) is what is invented that did not exist before, by the ruling of the sunnah. And in this there are several aspects:

The first: ﴿I am not a novelty among the messengers,﴾ meaning: I am not the first of them. So you should not deny my informing you that I am the messenger of Allah to you, nor deny my calling you to monotheism and my forbidding you to worship idols, for all the messengers were sent in this manner.

The second aspect: they asked him for great miracles and information about the unseen, and he said: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers.﴾ The meaning is that bringing these overpowering miracles and informing about these unseen matters is not within the power of humans, and I am of the kind of the messengers, and none of them was able to do what you want, so how could I be able to do it?

The third aspect: they used to criticize him for eating food and walking in the markets, and for his followers being poor. So he said: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers,﴾ and all of them were of this description and in this station. So these things do not discredit my prophethood, just as they do not discredit theirs.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿nor do I know what will be done with me or with you.﴾ In this there are several issues:

The first issue: in the interpretation of the verse there are two views:
One: that it be understood as referring to the affairs of this world.
Two: that it be understood as referring to the affairs of the Hereafter.

As for the first: there are several aspects:
The first: I do not know what my affair and your affair will come to, and who among us will be the victorious and who the defeated.
The second: Ibn ʿAbbas said, in the narration of al-Kalbi: When the trials intensified upon the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) in Makkah, he saw in a dream that he was migrating to a land with palm trees, plants and water. He recounted it to his companions and they rejoiced at that, seeing it as a relief from what they were suffering from the harm of the polytheists. Then they remained for a while without seeing any sign of that, so they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have not seen what you said, and when will we migrate to the land you saw in the dream?" The Prophet (ﷺ) remained silent, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿nor do I know what will be done with me or with you,﴾ which is a matter he saw in a dream; "and I only follow what Allah has revealed to me."
The third: al-Dahhak said: "I do not know what you will be commanded with, nor what I will be commanded with, in matters of obligations, laws, jihad, nor in trials and tests; I only warn you with what Allah has informed me of regarding the affairs of the Hereafter, in reward and punishment."
The fourth: The meaning is that he says: "I do not know what will be done with me in this world: will I die or will I be killed as the prophets before me were killed? And I do not know what will be done with you, O deniers: will you be struck with stones from the sky, or will you be swallowed up by the earth, or will there be done to you what was done to the rest of the nations?"

As for those who understood this verse as referring to the affairs of the Hereafter: it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists, the hypocrites and the Jews rejoiced and said: "How can we follow a prophet who does not know what will be done with him and with us?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed We have given you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 1] up to His saying: ﴿And that was with Allah a great success﴾ [al-Fath: 5]. Thus He clarified what will be done with him and with those who followed him, and this verse was abrogated (naskh: abrogation), and Allah humbled the noses of the hypocrites and the polytheists. Yet most of the scholars of verification (muhaqqiqun) regarded this view as far-fetched and argued against it with several aspects:

The first: the Prophet (ﷺ) must know about himself that he is a prophet, and whenever he knows he is a prophet, he knows that major sins do not proceed from him and that he is forgiven. And if that is so, it is impossible that he should be doubtful as to whether he is forgiven or not.
The second: there is no doubt that the prophets are of higher station than the saints. So when He said of them: ﴿Indeed, those who say "Our Lord is Allah" and then are steadfast, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13], how is it conceivable that the Messenger, who is the chief of the pious and the exemplar of the prophets and saints, would remain doubtful as to whether he is among the forgiven or among the punished?
The third: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah knows best where He places His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124], and what is meant by it is the perfection of his state and the utmost of his nearness to the presence of Allah, the Exalted. And one whose state is this, how is it fitting for him to remain doubtful as to whether he is among the punished or among the forgiven? So it is established that this view is weak.

The second issue: Ibn ʿAbbas's companion, the author of al-Kashshaf, said: It was read as (ma yaf'alu) with a fatha on the ya', meaning: Allah, exalted is He, does it. If they say: (ma yaf'alu) is affirmative and not negated, and the proper phrasing would have been: "what will be done with me and with you?" We say: The implied meaning is: "I do not know what will be done with me, and I do not know what will be done with you."

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me,﴾ meaning: I do not say a word nor do an act except in accordance with revelation. The opponents of qiyas (analogical reasoning) argued by this verse, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) said no word and did no act except by a text that Allah revealed to him, so it is obligatory that our situation be likewise.

The explanation of the first: the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾
The explanation of the second: the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿follow him﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and His saying: ﴿let those who oppose his command beware﴾ [al-Nur: 63].

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and I am only a plain warner.﴾ They used to demand from him astonishing miracles and information about the unseen, so He said: Say: ﴿I am only a plain warner.﴾ The one capable of those acts that lie beyond human power, and the one who knows those unseen things, is none other than Allah, glorified is He.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Have you considered: if this is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel bears witness to its like and believes, while you act arrogantly? Indeed Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ In this there are issues:

The first issue: the answer to the conditional is omitted, and the implied meaning is: it would be said: "If this Book is from Allah, then you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its truth, then you act arrogantly, you would be among the losers." Then this answer was omitted. A parallel to this is your saying: "If I do good to you and you do evil to me, and I turn toward you and you turn away from me, then you have wronged me." So here the implied meaning is: Tell me, if it is established that the Qur'an is from Allah because of the inability of creation to produce its like, and then you disbelieve in it, and there also occurs the testimony of the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel that it is a miracle from Allah, then if you act arrogantly and disbelieve, are you not the most astray of people and the most unjust? Know that the answer to the conditional may be omitted in some verses and may be mentioned in others. The omission is as in this verse, and as in His saying: ﴿And if a Qur'an by which mountains were moved, or the earth were split, or the dead were made to speak...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 31]. The mentioned case is as in His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who is more astray?﴾ [Fussilat: 52], and His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered: if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light?﴾ [al-Qasas: 71].

The second issue: They differed about what is meant by His saying: ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel,﴾ into two views:

The first, which is the view of most: that this witness is ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam. The author of al-Kashshaf narrated: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, he looked at his face and knew that it was not the face of a liar, and he examined it and became certain that he was the awaited Prophet (ﷺ). So he said to him: 'I will ask you about three things that none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise will eat? And does the child resemble its father or its mother?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west. As for the first food the people of Paradise will eat, it is the extra part of the fish's liver. As for the child: if the man's water precedes, the child resembles him, and if the woman's water precedes, the child resembles her.' He said: 'I testify that you are truly the Messenger of Allah.' Then he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander, and if they learn of my Islam before you ask them about me, they will slander me before you.' Then the Jews came, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: 'What sort of man is ʿAbd Allah among you?' They said: 'The best of us and the son of the best of us, our master and the son of our master, and our most knowledgeable and the son of our most knowledgeable.' He said: 'What do you think if ʿAbd Allah embraces Islam?' They said: 'May Allah protect him from that!' Then ʿAbd Allah came out and said: 'I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' They said: 'The worst of us and the son of the worst of us!' and they belittled him. He said: 'This is what I was afraid of, O Messenger of Allah.' Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: 'I have not heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to anyone walking on the earth that he is among the people of Paradise, except for ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam.' And concerning him was revealed: ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel bears witness to its like.﴾"

They said: Because his Islam was in Madinah two years before the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this surah is Meccan, so how is it possible to apply this Meccan verse to an event that occurred at the end of the Messenger of Allah's time in Madinah? Then the Exalted said: ﴿And this is a Book confirming in Arabic tongue﴾, that is: this Qur'an confirms the Book of Moses in that Muhammad is truly a Messenger from Allah. The saying of the Exalted ﴿in Arabic tongue﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state. Then He said: ﴿to warn those who did wrong﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: the polytheists of Makkah. In His saying "to warn" (li-tundhira) there are two readings: the "ta" (you) because of the frequency with which this meaning occurs in direct address, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿that you may warn by it, and a reminder for the believers﴾ [al-A'raf: 2]; and the "ya" (he/it) because the Book was mentioned earlier, so the warning is attributed to the Book, just as it is attributed to the Messenger, and in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1], up to His saying: ﴿to warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾ [al-Kahf: 2].

Then the Exalted said: ﴿and good tidings for the good-doers﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the better view is that His saying ﴿and good tidings﴾ is in the nominative position, and the meaning is: it is good tidings for the good-doers. He said: it is also permissible that it be in the accusative position, meaning: to warn those who did wrong, and (to give) good tidings to the good-doers. The sum of the speech is that the purpose of sending down this Book is to warn those who turn away and to give good tidings to those who obey.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 46, verses 13–14 (part 1 of 3):**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast – there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship; and his carrying and his weaning are thirty months. When he reaches his maturity and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that pleases You. And make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims."﴾ ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds; they will be among the companions of Paradise – the true promise which they were promised.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had established the proofs of tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) and prophethood, and had mentioned the doubts of the deniers and answered them, He then mentioned the path of the sincere believers and the verifiers, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast﴾. We have already mentioned the explanation of this phrase in surah al-Sajdah. The difference between the two places is that in surah al-Sajdah He mentioned that the angels descend and say: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve﴾ [Fussilat: 30]. Here, He removed the intermediary from between them and mentioned that ﴿there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. So when we combine the two verses, the result is that the angels convey this good news to them, and that the Truthful, glorified is He, also makes them hear this good news directly, without an intermediary.

Know that these verses indicate that whoever ﴿believed and did righteous deeds﴾ [Maryam: 60], after the resurrection, neither fear nor grief will befall them. For this reason, the people of verification said: On the Day of Resurrection, they will be safe from the terrors. Some of them said: The fear of punishment is removed from them, but the fear of majesty and awe never departs entirely from the servant. Do you not see that the angels, despite their high ranks and perfect infallibility, the fear does not leave them? He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They fear their Lord from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 50]. This matter has already been discussed exhaustively in many verses, among them His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103].

[Page 13]

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ The Mu'tazilah said: This verse indicates several matters:

First: His saying, ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise﴾. This conveys restriction (hasr, exclusivity), and this indicates that the companions of Paradise are only those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast. This indicates that the perpetrator of a major sin before repentance does not enter Paradise.

Second: His saying, ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾. This indicates the invalidity of the view of one who says that reward is bounty (fadl) and not recompense (jaza').

Third: His saying, ﴿for what they used to do﴾ indicates the affirmation of action for the servant.

Fourth: This indicates that an effect may occur in the state of the one who causes it, or that any effect may exist before that, as evidence that a prior action necessitated a later reward.

Fifth: The servant's being entitled to something from Allah, the greatest kind of this being kindness to parents. For this reason, He followed it with this meaning, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents﴾. The discussion of a parallel to this verse has already been presented in surah al-'Ankabut and surah Luqman. In it there are issues:

The first issue: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī recited (bi-wālidayhi iḥsānan), while the rest recited (ḥusnan).

Know that iḥsān (kindness) is the opposite of evil conduct (isā'ah), and ḥusn (goodness) is the opposite of ugliness (qubḥ). Whoever recited (iḥsānan) has as his evidence His saying in surah Bani Isra'il: ﴿And to parents, kindness﴾ [al-Isra': 23], and the meaning is: We commanded him to convey to them kindness. The argument for the second recitation is His saying in al-'Ankabut: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents﴾, and there is no disagreement about it. The intended meaning is also that We commanded him to convey to them a good action, except that He named that good action "goodness" by way of emphasis, as one says: "This man is knowledge and generosity." Ḥusnan is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), because the meaning of "And We have enjoined upon man regarding his parents" is: We commanded him to be good to them (yuḥsin ilayhimā) with kindness (iḥsānan).

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾. Concerning this there are issues:

The first issue: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī recited (kurhan) with a ḍamma on the kāf, while the rest recited it with a fatḥa. It is said: both are dialectal variants, like al-ḍaʿf and al-ḍuʿf, and al-faqr and al-fuqr; and among non-verbal nouns: al-daff and al-duff, and al-shahd and al-shuhd. Al-Wahidi said: al-kurh is a verbal noun from "karihtu al-shay'a, akrahuhu" (I disliked the thing), and al-karh is the noun, as if it were "the thing disliked." He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, while it is hateful to you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216], which is with a ḍamma. And He said: ﴿That you inherit women against their will﴾ [al-Nisa': 19], which is in the position of a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl). The second was not recited with other than a fatḥa. So whatever is a verbal noun or in the position of a circumstantial accusative, the fatḥa is better for it; and whatever is a noun, like "I went with it under compulsion (ʿalā kurh)," the ḍamma is better for it.

The second issue: The exegetes said: His mother carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty. It does not mean the beginning of pregnancy, for that is not a difficulty. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿When he covered her, she carried a light burden﴾ [al-A'raf: 189], meaning the beginning of pregnancy, for that is not a difficulty. The fetus is a drop (nuṭfah), a clot (ʿalaqah), and a lump of flesh (muḍghah). When it becomes heavy, then ﴿His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾ means the severity of labor pains.

The third issue: The verse indicates that the mother's right is greater, because He, exalted is He, first said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents﴾, mentioning both of them together, then He singled out the mother for mention, saying: ﴿His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾. This indicates that her right is greater, and that the hardships reaching her because of the child are greater. The reports on this subject are well known.

[Page 14]

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And his carrying and his weaning are thirty months﴾. Concerning this there are issues:

The first issue: This is from the omission of a modifier (ḥadhf al-muḍāf), and the estimate is: "And the period of his carrying and his weaning is thirty months." Al-Fiṣāl means weaning (al-fiṭām), which is separating him from milk. If it is said: The intended meaning is to specify the period of nursing, not weaning, so how is it expressed with fiṣāl? We say: Since nursing is followed by weaning and is fitting for it, because it ends and is completed by it, it is called fiṣāl.

The second issue: The verse indicates that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months. Because the total period of pregnancy and nursing is thirty months, and He said: ﴿Mothers nurse their children for two complete years﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233], if you subtract the two complete years, which are twenty-four months, from the thirty, the minimum period of pregnancy remains six months. It is reported from ʿUmar that a woman was brought before him who had given birth after six months, so he ordered her to be stoned. ʿAli said: There is no stoning upon her, and he mentioned the chain that we have mentioned. And from ʿUthmān that he intended to do that, so Ibn ʿAbbās recited this to him.

Know that reason and experience also indicate that the matter is so. The practitioners of experiments said: The formation of the fetus has a determined duration; when that duration is doubled, the fetus moves; when twice that total is added to it, the fetus separates from the mother. Let us suppose that its creation is completed in thirty days. When that duration is doubled until it becomes sixty, the fetus moves. When twice that total is added to it, which is one hundred and twenty, until the total becomes one hundred and eighty, which is six months, then the fetus separates. Let us suppose that its creation is completed in thirty-five days, so it moves at seventy days. When twice that is added to it, which is one hundred and forty days, the total becomes one hundred and eighty and ten days, which is seven months, and the child separates. Let us suppose that its creation is completed in forty days, so it moves at eighty days, and it separates at two hundred and forty days, which is eight months. Let us suppose that the creation is completed in forty-five days, so it moves at ninety days, and it separates at two hundred and seventy days, which is nine months. This is the calculation that the practitioners of experiments mentioned.

Galen said: I was very keen to investigate the durations of pregnancy, and I saw a woman who gave birth at one hundred and eighty-four nights. Abu ʿAli ibn Sina claimed that he witnessed that. So the minimum period of pregnancy, according to the explicit text of the Qur'an and according to medical experiments, has become one and the same thing, which is six months. As for the maximum period of pregnancy, there is nothing in the Qur'an indicating it. Abu ʿAli ibn Sina said in the sixth chapter of the ninth treatise of ʿUnwān al-Shifā' (The Cure): It reached me from a source in whom I had complete trust that a woman gave birth after the fourth year of pregnancy to a child whose teeth had grown, and he lived.

It is related from Aristotle that he said: The times of birth and gestation of animals are fixed except for man; sometimes a pregnant woman gives birth at seven months, and sometimes in the eighth. A child born in the eighth rarely lives, except in certain lands such as Egypt; and the usual is birth after the ninth month. The practitioners of experiments said: What we have said, that when the duration of formation is doubled the fetus moves, and when twice that is added to the total the fetus separates, we have said only approximately, not as an exact limit. For it may increase or decrease by days, because no proof has been established for this precise calculation; it is only an approximation mentioned on the basis of experience. And God knows best.

Then he said: The period in which the fetus's creation is completed is divided into parts:

The first: When the womb contains the semen and does not expel it outward, the semen turns around itself, contained within itself, and becomes like a sphere. Since it is in the nature of semen to be corrupted by movements, it therefore thickens at this time. It is fitting that the creation of the semen is from a substance that dries out by heat, if the purpose of it is the formation of the living being and the firmness of its parts. The semen becomes foam on the sixth day.

The second: The appearance of the three blood spots in it:

[Page 15]

The first is in the middle, and that is the place which, when its creation is completed, becomes the heart. The second is above, and that is the brain. The third is on the right, and that is the liver. Then these spots spread apart, and red threads appear between them, and that occurs after another three days, so the total becomes nine days.

The third: The blood spreads throughout the whole, so it becomes a clot (ʿalaqah). That happens after another six days, so the total becomes fifteen days.

The fourth: It becomes flesh, and the three organs have become distinct, and the moisture of the spinal cord has extended. That is completed in twelve days, so the total becomes twenty-seven days.

The fifth: The head separates from the shoulders, and the limbs separate from the ribs and the belly; sensation is distinguished in some parts and hidden in others. That is completed in another nine days, so the total becomes thirty-six days.

The sixth: The separation of these organs from one another is completed, and it becomes such that that sensation clearly appears. That is completed in another four days, so the total becomes forty days, and it may be delayed until forty-five days. He said: The minimum is thirty days. Thus these medical experiments became consistent with what the Truthful, the one whose word is believed, reported in his saying ﷺ: "The creation of one of you is gathered together in his mother's womb for forty days." The practitioners of experiments said: When a miscarriage after forty days is cut open, its substance is taken out and placed in cold water, something small with distinct limbs appears.

[Page 16]

**Third issue:** This verse indicates both the minimum period of pregnancy and the maximum period of breastfeeding. As for its indicating the minimum period of pregnancy, we have already explained that. As for its indicating the maximum period of breastfeeding, it is due to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And mothers suckle their children for two full years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233]. The jurists (fuqaha') have tied many rulings in jurisprudence (fiqh) to these two rules. Furthermore, once it is established that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, then, supposing a woman gives birth to a child within these months, her reputation remains protected from the accusation of fornication and indecency. And supposing that the maximum period of breastfeeding is what we have mentioned, then if nursing takes place after this period, it does not produce the legal consequences of breastfeeding, and thus the woman remains covered from strangers. At this point it becomes clear that the purpose of establishing the minimum pregnancy as six months and the maximum breastfeeding as two full years is to strive to ward off harms, indecencies, and all kinds of accusation against the woman. Glory be to Him, beneath every word of this noble Book are wondrous secrets and subtle treasures, and minds fall short of encompassing its perfection.

Al-Wahidi narrated in *al-Basit* from ʿIkrimah that he said: "If she carries [the child] for nine months, she nurses him for twenty-one months; and if she carries him for six months, she nurses him for twenty-four months." But the correct view is what we have already presented.

* * *

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿until, when he reaches his maturity (ashudd) and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents"﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

**First issue:** The exegetes (mufassirun) differed in interpreting *ashudd* (full maturity). Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of ʿAta', said: "It means eighteen years." Most exegetes hold that it is thirty-three years. Al-Farra' argued against this view, saying: "Forty is closer in sequence to thirty-three than to eighteen. Do you not see that you say, 'I took most of the wealth or all of it,' which is better than saying, 'I took the least of the wealth or all of it'? A similar example is His saying: ﴿Your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20]. Some of these divisions are close to one another, so it is the same here." Al-Zajjaj said: "The better view is to interpret it as thirty-three years, because this is the time when the human body reaches completion." I say: The thorough treatment of this subject is to say that the stages of age in living beings are three. This is because the body of a living being is formed only by innate moisture (al-ruṭūba al-gharīziyya) and innate heat (al-ḥarāra al-gharīziyya). There is no doubt that innate moisture predominates at the beginning of life and is deficient at the end of life, and the transition from increase to decrease cannot be conceived unless there is a state of balance in the middle of these two periods. Therefore it is established that the span of life is divided into three parts:

The first: innate moisture exceeds innate heat, and in this state the organs are capable of expanding in themselves by increase in length, breadth, and depth. This is the age of growth and development.

The second stage, which is the intermediate stage: innate moisture is sufficient to preserve innate heat, without increase or decrease. This is the age of standing still (al-wuqūf), which is the age of youth.

The third stage, which is the final stage: innate moisture falls short of sufficing to preserve innate heat. This deficiency is of two kinds:
The first is the hidden deficiency, which is the age of middle age (al-kuhūla).
The second is the apparent deficiency, which is the age of old age (al-shaykhūba). This is a known classification.

Then there is another premise here: the cycle of the moon is completed in a period of twenty-eight days and some. When we divide this period into four parts, each part is seven days. For this reason they measured the month by the four weeks, and these weeks have great effects on the variation of conditions in this world. Having understood this, we say: The researchers among the experimenters divided the period of growth and development into four weeks (asābīʿ, sg. sābūʿ), and at the end of each of these four weeks the human being undergoes a kind of change that leads to his completion. As for the end of the first week of life, his organs harden to some degree, his actions also gain some strength, his weak and fragile teeth are replaced by strong teeth, and the power of appetite in this week is stronger in digestion than before. As for the end of the second week, heat strengthens, moistures decrease, channels widen, the power of digestion increases, the organs grow strong, and they harden with sufficient strength and firmness, and seminal matter is generated in him. At this point the Shariah judges him to have reached puberty according to the opinion of al-Shafiʿi (may Allah be pleased with him). This is the truth from which there is no turning away, because at this time, when innate heat has become strong, moistures decrease, and the brain becomes balanced, the psychic faculties—thought and memory—are perfected. Therefore he is necessarily judged to have attained full intellectual maturity, and for this reason the Shariah ruled for puberty and the imposition of legal obligations. How excellent is the statement of the one who fixed legal puberty at fifteen years.

Know that from the attainment of this state there follow certain conditions in the outward body:
One of them: the separation of the tip of the nose (arnaba), because the innate moisture there decreases, and so the separation appears.
The second: the protrusion of the larynx (ḥanjara) and the thickening of the voice, because the heat that rises at that time widens the larynx, so it protrudes and the voice thickens.
The third: the change in the smell of the armpit, which is the putrid residue that the heart pushes to that place. This is because when the heat of the heart becomes strong, it is necessarily strong enough to ripen the matter and push it to the soft glandular flesh in the armpit.
The fourth: the growth of hair and the occurrence of nocturnal emission (iḥtilām). All of this is because heat has become strong, so it is able to generate the vapors that produce hair and to generate seminal matter. At this time desire is stirred in girls, their breasts swell, and their menstruation begins, all of this because the innate heat within them has become strong at the end of this week. As for the third week, the person enters the limit of completion, and beard grows for males, and their beauty and perfection increase. As for the fourth week, these conditions remain in him complete and increasing; and at the end of the fourth week, the final limit is that the increase no longer appears. As for the period of youth, which is the period of standing still, it is one week, so the total is thirty-five years. Since this period may either increase or decrease according to temperaments, the limit in this matter was set as forty years. This is the age at which the perfection suited to the human being is attained, both according to the Shariah and according to medicine. For at this time the actions of the natural faculties become somewhat quiet, the actions of the animal faculty reach their ultimate end, and the actions of the psychic faculty begin with strength and perfection. Having understood this premise, it becomes clear to you that the human being's reaching the time of *ashudd* is one thing, and his reaching forty is another. For his reaching the time of *ashudd* is an expression of arriving at the end of the age of growth and development, while his reaching forty is an expression of arriving at the end of the period of youth. From that time the natural and animal faculties begin to diminish, while the intellectual and rational faculty begins to reach completion. This is one of the things that indicates that the soul (nafs) is other than the body, for the body at forty begins to decline, whereas the soul from the time of forty begins to be perfected. If the soul were identical with the body, then the same thing would have perfection and deficiency at the same time, and that is impossible. What we have stated and summarized here is set down in the explicit wording of the Qur'an, for we have shown that at forty the perfections produced by the natural and animal faculties come to an end, while the perfections produced by the rational and intellectual faculties begin to be perfected. The proof of this is His saying: ﴿until, when he reaches his maturity and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents"﴾. This indicates that the human being's turning toward the world of servitude and occupation with obedience to Allah arises only from this time. This is an explicit statement that the rational, intellectual, rational-speaking psychic faculty begins to be perfected only from this time. Glory be to Him who placed in this Noble Book these noble and sacred secrets.

The exegetes said: "No prophet was ever sent except after forty years." I say: This is problematic with respect to Jesus, peace be upon him, for Allah made him a prophet from the beginning of his life. Nevertheless, it must be said: the usual pattern is that revelation did not come to him except after forty, and it was likewise in the case of our Messenger (ﷺ). It is narrated that when ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz reached forty years, he used to say: "O Allah, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing," up to the end of the supplication. It is also narrated that "Gabriel came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'The two guardian angels are commanded: Be gentle with My servant from the youth of his age; then when he reaches forty, it is said: Preserve him and make him firm.'" The narrator of this hadith, whenever he mentioned it, would weep until his beard was wet. It was related by al-Qadi in *al-Tafsir*.

**Second issue:** Know that His saying: ﴿until, when he reaches his maturity and reaches forty years﴾ indicates that the human being is like one who needs his parents' care for him until about this period. This is because the intellect is, in a sense, deficient, so he must have his parents' care in securing benefits and warding off calamities. It also contains a reminder that the blessings of the parents upon the child, after his entry into existence, extend to this long period, and this indicates that the parents' blessings are such that it is almost beyond the human being's capacity to repay them, except through supplication and good remembrance.

**Third issue:** Al-Wahidi relates from Ibn ʿAbbas and a great number of both earlier and later exegetes that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). They said: "The proof of this is that Allah has specified the pregnancy and weaning here by an amount which is known to vary, sometimes less and sometimes more, due to differences among people in these conditions. Therefore it is necessary that the intended person be one individual, so that it may be said that this specification is a report about his condition. It is possible, then, that Abu Bakr's pregnancy and weaning were of this amount."

Then He, may He be exalted, said in describing that person: ﴿until, when he reaches his maturity and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful"﴾.

[Page 18]

Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents. It is known that not every person says this statement, so the intended person in this verse must be a specific individual who said it. Abu Bakr said this statement at around this age, because he was two years and some months younger than the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) was sent at forty, and Abu Bakr was close to forty. He affirmed the Prophet (ﷺ) and believed in him. Thus it is established, by what we have mentioned, that these verses are suitable for Abu Bakr to be the one intended. Since this suitability is established, we say: we claim that he is the one intended by this verse. This is shown by the fact that at the end of this verse, He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds; they are among the companions of Paradise.﴾ This indicates that the one intended by this verse is the most excellent of creation, because the one from whom Allah accepts his best deeds and overlooks all his misdeeds must be among the most excellent and foremost of creation. The ummah (community) has agreed that the most excellent of creation after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is either Abu Bakr or ʿAli. It is not permissible for the one intended by this verse to be ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), because this verse fits only the one who uttered this statement upon reaching ashudd (full maturity) and near forty. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib was not in that condition, since he believed during his childhood or near childhood. Thus it is established that the one intended by this verse is Abu Bakr, and Allah knows best.
